policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The menu options need no target point; if a point is demanded anyway, point at the object the option names (the cube for C, D, E; the stick for A; the target for B and E would be the cube's destination, but prefer the cube). An episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory; first fill `method` from the demonstration steps, then choose by it. Rules, applied in whatever situation the policy stands in: - If `method` is `push`: choose C (close gripper and push the cube to the target). This is the only subgoal for a push episode. - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `none`: choose D (pick up the cube). - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `cube` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 40-60% on the cube and the gripper rise): choose E (place the cube onto the target). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `none`: choose A (pick up the peg). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `peg` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 20-25% on the stick and the gripper rise): choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). If a situation has no rule: if `method` cannot be told, decide by what the scene shows - fingers partly closed with the cube raised means E, fingers closed to about 20-25% with the stick raised means B; otherwise if the demonstration showed the stick held choose A, if it showed the cube lifted choose D, and if neither choose C. Never choose E without the cube in hand and never choose B without the peg in hand.

fields.name: method
fields.description: The way the demonstration moved the cube. At the first decision step, read it from the demonstration steps: `pick` if the cube is marked as held in the gripper while the gripper is well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed (about 40-60% open) and the cube is then released over the target; `hook` if the stick (peg) is marked as held in the gripper with fingers closed to about 20-25% and is dragged against the cube toward the target; `push` if the fingers close to about 0% at table height (height below about 0.04) and the cube slides to the target without ever being lifted or any stick being held. At every later step copy the value carried in unchanged; never write `unknown` after the first step. e.g. hook

fields.name: holding
fields.description: What the robot has in its fingers at this decision step. Write `none` at the first decision step (nothing has been executed yet). Write `cube` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the cube, close the fingers to about 40-60%, and rise again with the fingers still partly closed. Write `peg` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the stick, close the fingers to about 20-25%, and rise again with the fingers still closed. Write `none` if the fingers at this step are 100% open or closed to about 0%. If the execution steps show no grasp, copy the value carried in. e.g. peg
